name: Mackerel Uddamethi
subtitle: saraswat mackerel curry built on toasted urad dal and fenugreek, sour and slightly bitter

ingredients.qty: 4 mackerel, cleaned and cut into thick halves
ingredients.note: bangda; pomfret or seer also work
the methi; more than this turns the curry bitter

prepNotes: Rub the mackerel with 1/4 tsp turmeric and salt and leave 15 minutes; rinse and pat dry. This firms the flesh so it does not break up in the pot.
Soak the tamarind in 3 tbsp hot water and press out the pulp.
Have the masala fully ground before the fish goes anywhere near the heat — from that point the curry takes eight minutes.

steps.text: Warm 1 tbsp of the coconut oil and roast the urad dal over low heat 3 minutes until it turns reddish and smells nutty.
steps.tip: Urad dal keeps browning after you take it off the heat, so pull it a shade early.

steps.text: Add the fenugreek seeds and roast 30 seconds only, then the chillies and coriander powder for another minute.
steps.tip: Fenugreek turns acrid the moment it goes dark brown. Thirty seconds, not sixty.

steps.text: Grind the roasted mixture with the grated coconut, turmeric and 200ml water to a smooth, pourable paste.
Heat the remaining oil in a wide pan and soften the onion 5 minutes until translucent but not coloured.
Pour in the ground masala with another 150ml water, add the green chilli and salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer 6-7 minutes, stirring, until the raw coconut smell is gone and the surface glistens.
Slide in the mackerel in a single layer, spoon gravy over it, and cook 6 minutes without stirring.
steps.tip: Shake the pan by the handle instead of stirring — a spoon will shred the fish.

steps.text: Add the tamarind pulp, simmer 2 minutes more, and take it off the heat. Rest 10 minutes before serving with rice.
Scatter over the coriander leaves at the table.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat only to steaming, never boiling, or the mackerel falls apart. Not suitable for freezing.
